title: Susan Collins needs to answer to Maine veterans on healthcare
text:
The BDN Opinion section operates independently and does not set news policies or contribute to reporting or editing articles elsewhere in the newspaper or on bangordailynews.com
Melinda Swayne of Bryant Pond is a Navy veteran.
I served in the U.S. Navy for 26 years — from 1999 to 2025. In that time, I deployed to the Persian Gulf, Iraq, Japan and Bahrain. Today, I live in Bryant Pond with my husband, who is also a veteran.
Maine veterans like us put everything on the line to defend our country. Our national defense budget, which Sen. Susan Collins plays a key role in setting, should protect the people who serve, not be used as an ATM for her political donors.
That’s why, when I read the recent ProPublica investigation about the Collins 2020 campaign allegedly taking illegal money from a defense contractor, I felt deeply betrayed. Not just by Collins, but also by our current commander in chief who reportedly derailed the FBI’s recent investigation into whether or not our senator, who is supposed to work for Mainers, sold us out.
Now I want answers from Collins. Real answers, because Maine veterans deserve a senator who will fight for them.
In the Navy, I was a Naval Flight Officer and later transitioned to work in military medicine. Healthcare is a passion of mine. With Collins as chair of the Appropriations Committee, I’d like to know why VA healthcare is not fully funded, but Navatek is getting contracts that produce little of value.
The VA was created in 1930, and the U.S. has a history of caring for veterans that goes back much further than that. VA healthcare exists for one reason: to take care of the women and men who served their country in uniform. From battle wounds to mental health services, the VA promises to “honor America’s Veterans by providing exceptional healthcare that improves their health and well-being.”
It’s supposed to be there when veterans need it, with professionals who understand the unique needs of the people who served. So why are there severe staff shortages at the VA? Why do veterans have to deal with canceled or rescheduled appointments, delayed benefits, and longer wait times?
And that’s only talking about Susan Collins’ choices when it comes to healthcare for veterans. How about healthcare for the rest of Maine?
Collins cast a decisive vote to advance President Donald Trump’s budget reconciliation bill that gave over $1 trillion in tax cuts to the ultra-rich and cost Maine more than $4 billion in cuts to healthcare, nutrition assistance, and clean energy investments over the next 10 years. That bill slashes $2.7 billion from MaineCare, Maine’s Medicaid program, which provides healthcare to individuals and families with low income, children, older Mainers, and people with disabilities.
Collins seemingly won’t take responsibility for these massive healthcare cuts because of her final “no” vote on the bill. But I believe casting a key vote to keep the bill alive and then voting against it only once her vote apparently no longer mattered is playing political games.
I believe she’s hoping Mainers won’t notice as she allowed the diminishing of our healthcare to fund massive tax cuts for billionaires. But we’re not so easily fooled. I see her voicing symbolic opposition or “concern” when a bill will pass without her vote anyway, and offering support when Trump actually needs her vote.
The people of Maine need a senator who won’t enable a reckless president to drag us into new forever wars when we need healthcare, and good schools, and gas and groceries we can afford here at home. We’re smarter than that.

title: Four astronauts return to Earth after eight months in space
text:
CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — Four astronauts returned to Earth from the International Space Station on Thursday after hurrying there eight months ago to replace an ailing colleague and his crew.
SpaceX brought the U.S., French and Russian flyers back with a splashdown in the Pacific off the coast of Los Angeles.
NASA’s Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, France’s Sophie Adenot and Russia’s Andrey Fedyaev departed the orbiting lab on Wednesday, eager to reunite with their families after a lengthy separation. Their replacements arrived three weeks late because of capsule repairs, stalling this crew’s homecoming.
“We are so excited to be back on Planet Earth after an incredible mission on the International Space Station,” Meir radioed moments after splashing down. While still in orbit, she said the crew had “a lot of mixed, swirling emotions” and would miss the “extraordinary views of our home planet.”
Meir and her crew left the planet in February to replace four station occupants who were sent home early after one of them — NASA’s Mike Fincke, now retired — fell ill. It was NASA’s first medical evacuation in 65 years of human spaceflight.
Will his mustache disappear now that his mission is over?

title: Cooper Flagg and New Balance unveil logo with nod to Maine
text:
After nearly two years of professional partnership, Maine native Cooper Flagg and New Balance unveiled a new logo Thursday that will be used on all collaborative product lines.
The video announcement includes multiple nods to the Pine Tree State, including a shot of the basketball court at Nokomis Regional High School in Newport and a Maine license plate reading “FL4GG.”
The logo itself is a stylized “CF,” with the C resembling a pine tree, another nod to Flagg’s home state.
Flagg attended Nokomis as a high school freshman, earning Maine’s Gatorade Player of the Year in 2022 and helping the Warriors win the school’s first Class A championship. He then played two years at Montverde Academy in Florida and then a year of college basketball at Duke University.
In June 2025, Flagg was selected with the No. 1 overall pick in the NBA Draft by the Dallas Mavericks. He was named Rookie of the Year last season after averaging 21 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 1.2 steals per contest.
Flagg’s second season tips off Oct. 21 when the Mavericks play at the Houston Rockets.

title: Collapsed section of Old Town bridge will be demolished next week
text:
Demolition will begin next week on a section of the Old Town bridge that collapsed during construction on Aug. 14, injuring one person.
The new Llewellyn Estes Bridge was being built to carry Stillwater Avenue over the Stillwater River. The daytime collapse of one section was captured on video by a camera at a downstream dam.
The cause hasn’t been officially disclosed, but the reconstruction will use traditional steel girders in place of the fiber-reinforced polymer girders that were used in the collapsed section.
During the upcoming demolition, the temporary bridge that has been carrying traffic over the river at that point, will be closed periodically between the hours of 9 a.m. and 3 p.m. starting Tuesday, Oct. 13, and potentially continuing into the week of Oct. 19.
The exact timing of the closures, which are necessary because of how close the temporary bridge is to the collapsed span, will depend on “demolition operations, construction progress, weather conditions, and other site-specific factors,” Maine DOT said.
When the bridge is closed, Stillwater Avenue drivers will be detoured on a route that includes Bennoch Road, North Main Street, and College Avenue.
The bridge contractor, Reed & Reed, will work with a specialized demolition subcontractor to separate the failed span from the pier and abutment. The span will then be broken into smaller sections, lifted from the river and processed on land, Maine DOT said.

title: Crash in Lovell leaves one dead, another hospitalized
text:
LOVELL, Maine (WABI) - One person is dead and another is hospitalized after a head-on crash involving two vehicles in Lovell.
The crash happened just before 12 p.m. Thursday on Main Street, according to the Oxford County Sheriff’s Office.
Ivy Thomson, 25, who was driving one of the vehicles, died at the scene, the sheriff’s office said.
The other driver, Mark Farrington, 66, of Andover, was flown to a hospital with life-threatening injuries, officials said.
There were no passengers in either vehicle.
Anyone who witnessed the crash is asked to call the Oxford County Sheriff’s Office at (207) 743-9554.
